title: Grateful Dead Live at Allan Theater on 1971-10-29
source: Recording Info: SBD (7inch Master Reels@7.5ips 1/2trk) -> Cass (Tascam 122mkIII) -> Dat (3800/48k) Transfer Info: Dat (Sony D8) -> RME Hammerfall Digiface -> Sharp MV10 -> Samplitude v7.02 Professional -> SHN

ai_review.summary: Soundboard capture of a loose but high‑energy 1971 show highlighted by a monster 21‑minute Other One, though the mix is muffled and Keith’s keys dominate.
ai_review.review: The performance shines with an epic 21‑minute The Other One suite, adventurous sandwich transitions (Me & My Uncle → Deal) and strong renditions of Sugar Magnolia, Tennessee Jed and Playing in the Band. While the recording is a soundboard source, listeners note a muffled overall tone and Keith Godchaux’s organ/piano sitting too high in the mix, yet it remains listenable. The band’s autumn‑'71 energy is generally high, making this a fan‑favorite despite its sonic quirks.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers praise the musical performance (many 4–5 star comments) while noting moderate recording issues, yielding a strong combined rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Muffled overall sound; keyboards (Keith) overly forward in the mix; occasional clarity issues but generally listenable with no major dropouts.

standout_songs: Not Fade Away > Going Down the Road
show_quality.setlist_flow: Typical autumn‑'71 set with a solid first half and an adventurous second‑set jam suite (Other One → Me & My Uncle → Deal) plus classic transitions, showcasing a loose but funky groove.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Described as ripping, having fun vocalizations, and delivering strong guitar work especially on Playing in the Band and Tennessee Jed.
band_member_comments.Phil: Noted for tight interplay with Jerry on The Other One opener; overall solid bass foundation.
band_member_comments.Bob: Mixed feedback – one reviewer calls him "sucks" while others praise his rhythm and vocal parts on Sugar Magnolia.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith Godchaux is prominent in the mix, playing like a demon; his organ/piano adds energy despite being too front‑center.
